linux_model: Open-source, built into the kernel (i915/Xe drivers) — no separate install needed on modern kernels
bsd_model: Open-source, built into FreeBSD/OpenBSD graphics stack via the same DRM code shared with Linux
windows_note: Windows users get drivers directly from Intel
label: Official OS Repository / Built into Kernel
notes: Almost never needs a manual driver install on Linux/BSD — comes with the kernel/Mesa. Very old or very new Intel GPUs occasionally need a newer kernel than a stable-branch distro ships.

linux_model: Open-source AMDGPU driver, built into the kernel and Mesa; firmware blobs from linux-firmware package
bsd_model: Supported via the same DRM/amdgpu code on FreeBSD (drm-kmod port)
windows_note: Windows users get drivers directly from AMD
label: Official OS Repository / Built into Kernel
notes: Open-source AMDGPU is generally excellent and preinstalled. Very recent GPU releases can need a newer kernel/Mesa than what a stable distro branch ships.

linux_model: Proprietary driver from NVIDIA (packaged by most distros) OR the open-source Nouveau driver (built into the kernel, less performant)
bsd_model: FreeBSD packages an NVIDIA driver port; OpenBSD relies mainly on the open Nouveau driver with more limited support
windows_note: Windows users get drivers directly from NVIDIA
label: Official Manufacturer + Official OS Repository
notes: Distro package managers (e.g. Ubuntu's 'Additional Drivers', Pop!_OS's NVIDIA ISO, Fedora via RPM Fusion) are usually the easiest way to install the proprietary driver rather than NVIDIA's raw .run installer.

linux_model: Open-source iwlwifi kernel driver; requires proprietary firmware blobs from linux-firmware
bsd_model: FreeBSD supports many Intel Wi-Fi chips via iwlwifi-compatible drivers/ports; OpenBSD has native iwm/iwn drivers
windows_note: Windows users get drivers via Windows Update or Intel directly
label: Built into Kernel + Firmware Package
notes: Almost always works out of the box if the distro includes non-free firmware (some strictly-free distros like Guix exclude it by policy, which can leave Wi-Fi non-functional).

device_category: Wi-Fi (Realtek chipsets, common in budget laptops/USB adapters)
linux_model: Mixed: some chips are in-kernel, many newer ones need out-of-tree community drivers
bsd_model: Support is inconsistent; check the specific BSD's hardware compatibility list before relying on Realtek Wi-Fi
windows_note: Windows users get drivers via Windows Update or Realtek directly
label: Mixed: Built into Kernel / Community Resource
notes: Realtek Wi-Fi is one of the most common sources of Linux hardware friction — always check a specific chipset model (e.g. RTL8821CE) against community driver repos before buying or installing.

device_category: Wi-Fi (common in older MacBooks and some laptops)
linux_model: The 'broadcom-sta' (wl) proprietary driver or open-source brcmfmac/brcmsmac, depending on chip generation
bsd_model: FreeBSD has some Broadcom support via if_bwn; coverage varies by chip
windows_note: Windows users get drivers via Windows Update or Broadcom/OEM directly
label: Mixed: Official OS Repository / Community Resource
notes: Ubuntu and Debian package the proprietary broadcom-sta driver in their 'restricted/non-free' repos for many older Broadcom chips.

linux_model: Open-source mt76 driver family, built into the kernel for most current MediaTek Wi-Fi chips
bsd_model: Support is limited and chip-dependent; check hardware notes carefully
windows_note: Windows users get drivers via Windows Update or MediaTek/OEM directly
label: Built into Kernel
notes: Generally good support on recent kernels; very new MediaTek Wi-Fi 6E/7 chips can need a newer kernel than a stable-branch distro ships at first.

linux_model: CUPS (Common Unix Printing System) with driverless IPP Everywhere support for most modern printers, plus manufacturer-supplied PPDs for older models
bsd_model: CUPS is also the standard printing system on FreeBSD/OpenBSD
windows_note: Windows users typically install a manufacturer driver package
label: Official OS Repository (CUPS) + Official Manufacturer (older models)
notes: Most printers made in the last ~10 years work 'driverless' via IPP Everywhere/AirPrint standards with zero setup. Older or specialty printers may need a manufacturer-specific driver package.

linux_model: fwupd (LVFS — Linux Vendor Firmware Service) delivers many vendor firmware updates directly, when supported
bsd_model: Not commonly integrated; firmware updates are typically done via manufacturer tools or a Windows/DOS boot
windows_note: Most OEMs still primarily ship firmware update tools for Windows
label: Official OS Repository (fwupd/LVFS) + Official Manufacturer
notes: Not every motherboard/laptop vendor participates in LVFS — check whether your specific model is listed before relying on it; otherwise a manufacturer's own (often Windows-only) tool may be required.
